methodological_rigor.justification: HOVON-902 (NCT04139252) is a prospective, multicenter (46 Dutch centers), national noninterventional cohort with prespecified statistical analysis plan. PhasED-Seq with a validated 95% LoD of 0.7 ppm is applied to 134 eligible patients with 99% successful phased-variant identification. Multivariable Cox regression adjusts for IPI and EOT PET-CT; PPV/NPV/sensitivity/specificity are compared with McNemar's test with Holm adjustment and GEE logistic regression with bootstrap CIs. Limitations include PET-CT not centrally reviewed, sample-level sensitivity lower than prior reports due to plasma volume and storage, some PFS events unrelated to lymphoma counted as events, and COVID-era protocol deviations (all acknowledged).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The study demonstrates that EOT ctDNA-MRD via PhasED-Seq provides independent prognostic information beyond IPI and PET-CT in uniformly treated first-line LBCL, with dramatic separation (3-year PFS 17% vs 85%, OS 43% vs 92%). MRD-positive non-CMR patients have 0% 3-year PFS, identifying a clear high-risk subset for trial enrichment. Findings align with NCCN guidance (v3.2025, category 2B) and inform ongoing MRD-directed trials (ALPHA3, SHORTEN-ctDNA). Oxford LoE 2b for a prospective prognostic cohort.

reporting_quality.justification: The work is a prognostic biomarker validation study, so REMARK is the applicable standard. Key items are addressed: clear patient flow (CONSORT-style Fig 1A), detailed inclusion/exclusion, biomarker assay description (PhasED-Seq with validated LoD), prespecified SAP, multivariable modeling, and test performance metrics with confidence intervals. Study registration (NCT04139252) and full protocol in supplement. However, REMARK adherence is not explicitly stated, and patient-level data/code are not indicated as openly shared.

novelty_literature.justification: Although PhasED-Seq has been described (Kurtz 2021) and EOT ctDNA-MRD prognostic value was recently reported in a pooled trial analysis (Roschewski 2025, ref 13), this work is the first prospective validation in a uniformly treated, real-world national cohort with standard R-CHOP/DA-EPOCH-R and demonstrates superior PPV vs PET-CT (68% vs 56%) and independent prognostic value across CMR/non-CMR subgroups. The demonstration of feasibility in 46 academic and community centers also adds novelty for clinical implementation.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written with logical flow from patient selection through subgroup analyses, effective use of hazard ratios with very small p-values, and explicit comparison to prior literature (Kumar, Nijland, Roschewski). Figures 1-4 and supplementary materials communicate prognostic performance, PET-CT vs MRD comparisons, and relapse timing effectively. Limitations are candidly presented.

key_strengths: Prospective national multicenter (46 sites) real-world validation of PhasED-Seq EOT ctDNA-MRD in uniformly treated first-line LBCL
99% successful phased-variant identification using tissue or pretreatment plasma
Strong independent prognostic value beyond IPI and PET-CT (PFS HR 9.8, OS HR 7.7)
Superior PPV vs PET-CT (68% vs 56%) with similar NPV, supporting adjudication of PET-positive cases
Identification of ultra-high-risk MRD+/non-CMR subgroup (0% 3-year PFS) for trial enrichment
key_concerns: EOT PET-CT scans not centrally reviewed, introducing interpretation variability
Sample-level sensitivity lower than in some published reports due to plasma volume and storage
Some deaths unrelated to lymphoma counted as PFS events, which may affect small-subgroup estimates
Some MRD samples collected during additional rituximab; potential effect on clearance not quantified
REMARK checklist not explicitly cited; patient-level data/code not openly shared
chief_reviewer.rationale: A well-executed prospective real-world validation of ctDNA-MRD with strong prognostic performance and direct clinical implications; appropriate for a high-impact tier-1 hematology/oncology journal with minor revisions.
